A guide to Media over QUIC

MoQ for the Curious

On this page
Where to beginA protocol still taking shapeMaintenance and contributions

MoQ for the Curious explains how Media over QUIC delivers live content: how publishers name it, relays distribute it, and players keep it useful when the network slows.

We’ll introduce the networking and media concepts as we need them. To see how they fit together, we’ll follow an online lecture from the moment a student joins to the moment they hear the lecturer.

This book is inspired by WebRTC for the Curious and its approach to explaining how the pieces of a real-time communication system fit together.

Start reading: What, Why and How →

Where to begin

Start with the first chapter for an introduction and a comparison with WebRTC. Continue in order to follow the lecture through networking, subscriptions, relays, and playback. If you already know the basics, use Your First MoQ System to find demos and libraries to start with. The glossary explains unfamiliar terms along the way.

A protocol still taking shape

This edition uses MOQT draft-21, published September 8, 2026, as its IETF baseline. Implementation examples are labeled separately from protocol requirements.

The draft is useful reading alongside the book. Start with its motivation section, then follow the content model and protocol behavior before looking up individual message fields.

Initial research was completed on September 16, 2026, with a technical fact-check on September 22, 2026. Each chapter links to primary sources; the references explain the source policy and limitations. Example latency values are teaching aids, not benchmarks, and the upstream walkthrough commands have not been executed for this guide.

Maintenance and contributions

This book is maintained by @pham-tuan-binh. Corrections, clearer explanations, and new examples are welcome. The GitHub repository and contribution guide explain how to edit and build the book. You can submit a pull request directly, or email binhpham@binhph.am to suggest a change or ask for an update.
